body:
I realize this hasn't been done for 1900 years, but what is the procedure
for adding a new book to the Bible?  I know it is possible, as the New
Testament was added to what was previously considered the sacred,
unalterable Torah or Old Testament, then the Book of Revelation was
added to the sacred, unalterable gospels of Jebus' disciples.  So it must
be possible to add new books past Revelation, so what is the procedure?

I'm lobbying to include the famous 1995 essay "Industrial Society and Its
Future," also known as the "Unabomber Manifesto" by St. Theodore Kaczynski.
St. Ted is truly a Prophet of Gawd and his divinely-inspired revelation
deserves inclusion in the Bible, IMHO.  If his tendency towards violence
may seem to preclude the inclusion of his essay, let me just remind y'all
that parts of the Bible are filled with the most horrific calls to
violence, and since they have never been formally removed I interpret
that as tacit approval of the violence they endorse.

So what do I do?  Do I have to bribe an archbishop or suck the pope's
cock to get the Manifesto included?  Or is it like amending the
constitution where I have to formally propose it and then have it
ratified by 3/4 of xian denominations within a certain period of time?
